title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A/S is an abelian scheme of relative dimension g over a base of characteristic p>0, assumed ordinary (fibrewise or 'partout'). This continues the previous page, which split H = D^1(A/S) = H^1_dR(A/S) into H^0 = t_A^vee (that is, omega_A = f_*Omega^1) and H^1 = t_{A*} = R^1f_*O_A = Lie(A*). The previous page then asked for functorial stratifications (crystal structures) on the two pieces, and concluded that the position of the Hodge filtration relative to the stratification gives no infinitesimal classification in characteristic p.

On this page Grothendieck works out the ordinary case.

(1) Splitting. For ordinary A there is a canonical splitting D^1(A/S) = t_A^vee (+) t_{A*}. In modern terms, the conjugate filtration (Cartier) is transversal to the Hodge filtration exactly when A is ordinary. The conjugate sub-bundle F*R^1f_*O then gives a complement to omega_A.

(2) Trivialisation of the tangent spaces. One has t_A = L_A (x)_{F_p} O_S and t_{A*} = L_{A*} (x)_{F_p} O_S. Here L_A and L_{A*} are étale sheaves of F_p-vector spaces, locally free of rank g. They are the fixed points of the p-linear Hasse–Witt / Frobenius map, which is bijective in the ordinary case (Lang's theorem, i.e. a unit-root F-module of level 0).

(3) Identification over a perfect field k. Using Artin–Schreier, L_{A*} = H^1(A,O_A)^F = H^1_et(A,Z/p) = Hom(_pA, Z/p) = _pA(k)^vee, and symmetrically L_A(k) = _pA*(k)^vee. Hence:
- t_A^vee = _pA*(k) (x)_{F_p} k;
- t_{A*} = _pA(k)^vee (x)_{F_p} k.
In modern terms: ω_A is identified with the character group of the multiplicative part tensored with k, and Lie(A*) with the dual of the étale part of A[p]. These are the Serre–Tate / Dwork canonical coordinates at level p.

(4) Arbitrary S. Ordinarity implies that _pA -> S factors uniquely as _pA -> (_pA)_et -> S. The first map is finite locally free, radicial and surjective (connected-étale sequence, with multiplicative connected part); the second is finite étale.

The next page then gives L_A = ((_pA*)_et)^vee and L_{A*} = ((_pA)_et)^vee. It also studies the polarization class in Λ^2 D^1 and its tangent map t_A -> t_{A*}, which descends to (_pA)_et -> (_pA*)_et.

Purpose: testing whether a canonical decomposition plus stratification could classify deformations. In the ordinary case everything is governed by the étale part of _pA, foreshadowing Serre–Tate theory and unit-root crystals.
errors: Over a perfect but not algebraically closed k, the chain H^1(A,O_A)^F = H^1_et(A,Z/p) = Hom(_pA,Z/p) = _pA(k)^vee is not literally correct. The Artin–Schreier sequence contributes k/(F-1)k and H^1(k,Z/p). Also F-fixed points of t_{A*} need not have F_p-dimension g before passing to k-bar. The formulas are correct for k algebraically closed, or when read as étale sheaves. The next page repairs this with the sheaf version L_{A*} = ((_pA)_et)^vee.

The splitting D^1 = t_A^vee + t_{A*} is not horizontal for the Gauss–Manin connection: omega_A is not stable, since Kodaira–Spencer is generically nonzero. This is implicitly consistent with the previous page's remark but is not stated here.
Notation slip: '$\mathfrak{L}_{A^*}(\mathrm{k})$' was first written with a struck-out symbol. This is harmless.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard material on ordinary abelian varieties: the Hodge/conjugate splitting, unit-root trivialisation and connected–étale decomposition. All of it is well documented through Serre–Tate, Dwork, Katz and Deligne. It is historically mildly interesting as Grothendieck's c.1969 exploration of whether such splittings plus crystal structures could classify deformations, but there is no new result or connection.
